## Findings ledger
- [C3.DOC1.F1] The article qualifies the proposed common pattern of strong AUKUS bipartisanship: support is broad but not uniform, with internal opposition in Australia and unresolved US congressional resistance; a uniform template would erase these institutional and political differences — dim: comparison_limits — case: Australia, United States — criterion: Does each partner exhibit equivalent bipartisan support and implementation? — limit: context/comparability — pattern-tested: AUKUS partner states uniformly sustain strong bipartisan support — anchor: "To date bipartisan support for AUKUS remains strong." — doc: aukus — confidence: high. Additional support uses anchor-b: "Fifty of 800 grassroots Labor branches and left-aligned unions passed motions opposing AUKUS and nuclear-powered submarine acquisition." — doc-b: aukus. Further support uses anchor-c: "Republican members of the US Senate Armed Services Committee moved to block legislation enabling the sale of Virginia-class submarines to Australia." — doc-c: aukus
- [C3.DOC1.F2] The text contrasts formal regulatory authorization with effective industrial and political outcomes: the South Korean decree took effect, but its defence-export effect is only potential, so the June Eximbank capital proposal and December decree cannot be treated as stages of one identified amendment — dim: comparison_limits — case: South Korea — criterion: Can formal policy status be equated with effective implementation and outcome? — limit: comparability — pattern-tested: a proposal and a later effective decree are the same policy instrument and establish realized effects — anchor: "In response to industry calls for legislative amendments, in June 2023 the government proposed to increase the lender’s statutory capital limit." — doc: aukus — confidence: high. Additional support uses anchor-b: "The revised Enforcement Decree of the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act passed the National Assembly, coming into effect in December 2023" — doc-b: aukus. Further support uses anchor-c: "This institutional development potentially furthers South Korea’s defence exports, dubbed ‘K-Defense`, and dispels concerns that large-scale exports risk being annulled due to the bank’s lack of financial support." — doc-c: aukus
- [C3.DOC1.F3] Japan’s defence-export context is not equivalent to South Korea’s or the AUKUS members’: longstanding domestic export controls restricted transfers and contributed to a small defence industry, while revised guidelines were only pledged in July 2023 — dim: comparison_limits — case: Japan — criterion: Do partner states have comparable institutional conditions for defence-industrial participation? — limit: context/comparability — pattern-tested: AUKUS-related partners face equivalent regulatory conditions for defence exports and industrial expansion — anchor: "For decades, Japan’s export control policy, called the ‘Three Principles on Arms Export’, has constrained the defence industry to scale up production." — doc: aukus — confidence: high. Additional support uses anchor-b: "In July 2023, however, the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) and its long-standing coalition partner Komeito pledged that the government would push through revised guidelines" — doc-b: aukus

sections_inspected: AUKUS, bipartisanship, and the regulatory control
scope_outcomes.criterion: Retain source-supported exceptions, contextual differences, formal-versus-effective distinctions, and explicitly unavailable or out-of-scope comparison cells.
scope_outcomes.basis: The inspected sections contain explicit qualifications to common patterns, differences in national regulatory contexts, a formal/effective distinction in the South Korean measures, and an explicit statement that regional conflict effects are beyond scope.
limitations: The full article was supplied, but the assessment records the sections and passages specifically inspected for this dimension.
The source does not identify whether the June 2023 Eximbank proposal and December 2023 Enforcement Decree are the same instrument.
The source does not provide equivalent evidence on informal practice, cultural meaning, translation effects, or realized outcomes across all cases.

evidence_state.coverage_basis: reader/reviewer report; source bytes do not establish inspection or completeness
blocking_issues: Findings lost anchor evidence; this does not establish absence
